panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 8 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H). A: This is a gross whole-body fetal specimen in a case report specifically about Apert syndrome. The caption and in-text discussion identify multiple characteristic craniofacial, limb, palatal, and genital abnormalities. B: Prenatal ultrasound images in the Apert syndrome case demonstrate craniofacial abnormalities, including abnormal skull shape and facial dysmorphism. C: The prenatal ultrasound panel is specifically captioned as showing fetal hand syndactyly in Apert syndrome. D: The fetal ultrasound demonstrates the characteristic syndactyly described in the caption for Apert syndrome. E: The caption assigns ambiguous external genital organs and median fusion of the lower extremities to this fetal Apert syndrome case; no allowed vocabulary term directly matches the principal finding. F: The gross postmortem head and brain specimen is directly described in the Apert syndrome case caption as showing craniosynostosis and...
panels.attribution_text: Varlas et al. Emphasis on Early Prenatal Diagnosis and Perinatal Outcomes Analysis of Apert Syndrome.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland) 2024. doi:10.3390/diagnostics14141480. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasonographic and macroscopic findings—fetal cranium abnormalities (acrocephaly and brachycephaly), prominent forehead, nasal bone hypoplasia, facial dysmorphism (flat midface, hypertelorism, exorbitism), cleft lip and palate and low-set ears, hands syndactyly, feet syndactyly type IVa at all fingers, with median fusion of the low extremities, ambiguous external genital organs. A gross examination of the head and brain revealed craniosynostosis, hypertelorism, exorbitism, hypoplastic nose, pharynx abnormality, gyral anomalies, hypoplastic white matter, and heterotopic gray matter (personal collection) [24].
in_text_mentions: ilateral exophthalmos, low-set ears, small and flat nose, and cleft palate (in one-third of cases). In the conditions of a hypoplastic or malformed pharynx, severe respiratory problems can be associated. During the prenatal examination, possible bone abnormalities can be identified, such as syndactyly present both in the hands and feet, and it is necessary to establish the type of syndactyly (often “mitten-like” hand). Other possible anomalies in the hands and feet that can be identified are the absence of the middle phalanges and absent or supernumerary carpal/tarsal bones [22,23] (Figure 1).
